features.feature_value: Seeing both versions pushed them to be fair and focus on whether the exchange is productive dialogue rather than their own priors.
features.evidence_span: "Seeing both helped me be fair" ... "focus less on what I thought and more on if it was productive dialogue."
features.rationale: The reflection explicitly credits viewing both versions for shifting attention toward fairness and productive-dialogue criteria.

features.feature_value: Used a “fair, respectful, constructive dialogue” goal and considered perceptions of opposing viewers when deciding.
features.evidence_span: "importance of having a fair and respectful platform" ... "The goal should be to encourage constructive dialogue rather than division."
features.rationale: They describe decision criteria grounded in respect/constructiveness and framing it as avoiding division.

features.feature_value: Removed pairs mostly because they appeared vitriolic/hostile; expected facts rather than hostile opinions.
features.evidence_span: "I removed most pairs because they were just vitriolic comments" ... "I was expecting facts not hostile opinions."
features.rationale: Their removal rationale is directly tied to detecting vitriol/hostility.

features.feature_value: Treats profanity/vulgar language as an automatic disqualifier that triggers animosity and arguments.
features.evidence_span: "I immediately will not allow any post that includes profanity and vulgar language." ... "That right there will cause and trigger animosities"
features.rationale: They specify an immediate rule linking profanity to expected negative dynamics.

features.feature_value: Removed posts using offensive language or targeting a specific user; kept non-personal belief statements.
features.evidence_span: "I removed posts that used offensive language or that were targeting a specific user." ... "Any statements ... I kept."
features.rationale: They articulate concrete keep/remove boundaries around offensiveness and directed targeting.

features.feature_value: Swear words alone weren’t decisive; the key criterion was whether anyone was attacked.
features.evidence_span: "Curse words aren't really an issue" ... "but no one should be attacked."
features.rationale: They distinguish profanity tolerance from the prohibition on attacking people/“either side.”

features.feature_value: Compared which version looked rational vs name-calling to judge whether discussion could remain substantive or devolve.
features.evidence_span: "there were times when one seemed rational and the other seemed more like name calling" ... "could have an actual discussion"
features.rationale: They describe an explicit comparison strategy using rationality vs name-calling cues to anticipate devolution.
